source.title: What is the role of memorization in Continual Learning?
source.authors: Jȩdrzej Kozal; Jan Wasilewski; Alif Ashrafee; Bartosz Krawczyk; Michal Wo'zniak

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies memorization and forgetting in continual learning. Its experiments do not test the listed same-distribution generalization claims, and it does not use those claims as a tool.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on random-label fitting and memorization in generalization, but reports no new results testing those claims. Its own results concern memorization scores and continual-learning performance.
record.test_reason: The study measures per-example memorization scores, retention during continual learning, and replay-buffer performance. It does not test any listed version. In particular, replay selection using a training-iteration proxy does not test V8's removal of the most memorized examples followed by retraining against equal-sized random removal.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly matches the authors' conclusion: they argue that memorization is necessary to approach full-memory continual-learning performance, while regular-example retention matters more at low memory budgets. Qualify the evidence: scores were computed under stationary training, actual incremental memorization was not identified, and gains from adding 10% high-proxy examples in Table 3 were smaller than the reported standard deviations.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines memorization and forgetting in continual learning, not the original same-distribution generalization methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report outcomes varying with number of classes, model depth and width, buffer access, continual-learning method, and buffer size.

fits_no_version.finding: Memorization scores increase with class count; the authors report a stronger class-count effect than sample-count effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dataset composition changes per-example memorization scores in the tested stationary-training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Deeper models have lower memorization scores while overfitting; increasing width quickly saturates the mean score while increasing the highest scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ResNet depth and width affect memorization-score distributions on CIFAR100.

fits_no_version.finding: Accuracy on examples with high stationary memorization scores declines during continual learning, with retention depending on replay access and training method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retention of examples selected by stationary memorization scores depends on the continual-learning setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes using representations learned from other tasks classify a substantial portion of high-score examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High stationary memorization scores need not identify examples actually memorized during incremental training.

fits_no_version.finding: Training iteration correlates moderately with original memorization scores: Pearson 0.594, Spearman 0.597 and Kendall 0.427.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late stable learning provides a proxy for per-example memorization in the tested setting.

fits_no_version.finding: With buffers of 500, bottom-k and middle-k proxy-score policies outperform top-k selection on all three benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under small replay budgets, prioritizing lower proxy-score examples improves continual-learning accuracy relative to prioritizing higher-score examples.

record.problems: The authors note that memorization dynamics may vary with architecture, training procedure, hyperparameter selection, augmentation, regularization, and data repetition. Most experiments use CIFAR datasets and reduced ResNet18; some memorization plots lack error bars. Offline stationary-training memorization scores may not identify examples actually memorized during incremental training.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Several figure trends have no numeric values in the text and are recorded as text-described outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning, including recovery through broader tuning or optimizer changes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing the most memorized training examples and retraining, compared with removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No listed version receives a verdict. Using Feldman's estimator does not itself test V8. Likewise, using AdamW for probes, fixed batch sizes, or augmentation does not test optimizer, batch-size, or dropout effects.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance under the same recipe.
Test error after widening beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error on images.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Large-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the train-test gap.
Removing the most memorized training examples and retraining.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR100 subsets with differing numbers of classes; memorization scores measured on samples from the first 10 classes.
rows.measure: Distribution of memorization scores; the text states scores are lower as the number of classes gets smaller.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend but does not provide numeric values in the text.
rows.check: The subject is reduced ResNet18. Class-count effects on memorization scores do not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 subsets at different fractions of the original dataset size; memorization score measured.
rows.measure: Mean memorization scores and fraction of samples above memorization scores 0.25 and 0.1.
rows.note: The authors state that number of classes has a stronger influence than reduced sample count; plot values are not transcribed in the text.
rows.check: The subject is reduced ResNet18. Dataset-size effects on memorization scores do not establish random-label fitting or held-out generalization.

rows.subject: ResNet34 and ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Memorization scores measured after training on the full CIFAR100 dataset.
rows.measure: Memorization score distribution; scores decrease significantly as network depth increases, with both models reported to overfit.
rows.note: No numeric comparison is given in the text.
rows.check: Depth-dependent memorization scores and qualitative overfitting do not test width-dependent test error or convolutional versus fully connected performance.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Width multiplier varied while training on full CIFAR100; memorization scores measured.

conditions.value: different width multipliers; exact values not stated in this section

rows.measure: Mean memorization score and scores among the highest-memorization samples; mean score quickly saturates as width increases, with a visible increase among the highest-scoring samples.
rows.note: No numeric values are given in the text.
rows.check: Appendix I identifies width multipliers 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and the full-width baseline. The outcome is memorization score, with no test-error curve or established interpolation threshold; it cannot test V2.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained incrementally on Seq-Cifar100 with reservoir sampling and a buffer of size 500; tracked accuracy on samples with offline memorization scores above 0.25.
rows.measure: Accuracy on high-memorization training samples declined significantly after training on two subsequent tasks, then at a similar rate to test-set accuracy.
rows.note: The figure reports averaged results over 5 runs; numerical accuracies are not stated in text.
rows.check: The subject is reduced ResNet18. Retention of examples selected by stationary-training scores does not test random-label capacity or targeted-removal effects on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained incrementally with unlimited access to past-task memory; tracked accuracy on samples with offline memorization scores above 0.25.
rows.measure: Accuracy on high-memorization samples slowly decreased but remained high throughout training.
rows.note: The figure reports averaged results over 5 runs; numerical accuracies are not stated in text.
rows.check: The subject is reduced ResNet18. High accuracy on selected training examples with full replay access does not establish V1 or V8.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Learning without Forgetting (LwF), without a rehearsal buffer; tracked accuracy on samples with offline memorization scores above 0.25.
rows.measure: Accuracy on high-memorization samples declined significantly after the data-distribution change and was lower than test-set accuracy on newly introduced tasks.
rows.note: The authors state that the accuracy does not drop instantly to zero. Figure results averaged over 5 runs.
rows.check: The subject is reduced ResNet18. LwF's distillation regularization is not dropout, and this experiment does not test any listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Linear probes trained on frozen representations from incremental training; evaluated on task 5 samples selected by offline memorization score threshold.
rows.measure: Linear-probe accuracy on high-memorization samples showed the same dynamic as on test data; probes on representations from other tasks classified a substantial portion of those samples.
rows.note: The authors caution that offline scores do not necessarily identify samples actually memorized during incremental training.
rows.check: Specify reduced ResNet18 trained incrementally with SGD and linear probes trained with AdamW. There is no optimizer comparison. The authors caution that stationary scores need not identify examples memorized during incremental training.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation between training iteration and original memorization score.
rows.note: This measures association with memorization score, not the train-test gap.
rows.check: Change observed to cannot_determine relative to the listed versions. These correlations validate a memorization proxy, not a generalization-gap measure. Appendix B identifies CIFAR100 and 150 sampled examples for the original-score comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared buffer policies using proxy memorization scores on Split-CIFAR100 with buffer size 500.
rows.measure: Test accuracy: bottom-k 25.88±1.14; middle-k 23.62±1.07; top-k 17.28±1.19; reservoir 22.07±0.84.
rows.note: Continual-learning buffer policy results, not same-distribution generalization.
rows.check: The values match Table 1. These are comparisons of the study's proposed replay policies using proxy scores, not V8's targeted training-set removal and retraining experiment.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy for buffer policies using proxy memorization scores on Split-TinyImageNet with buffer size 500.
rows.measure: Test accuracy: bottom-k 7.85±0.29; middle-k 7.11±0.57; top-k 5.18±0.13; reservoir 6.38±0.62.
rows.note: Continual-learning buffer policy results, not same-distribution generalization.
rows.check: The values match Table 1. These measure proposed replay-policy performance, not removal of examples ranked by inclusion-based memorization.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy for buffer policies using proxy memorization scores on Split-CIFAR10 with buffer size 500.
rows.measure: Test accuracy: bottom-k 56.04±4.80; middle-k 55.96±4.62; top-k 41.16±7.38; reservoir 55.18±6.59.
rows.note: Continual-learning buffer policy results, not same-distribution generalization.
rows.check: The values match Table 1. These measure proposed replay-policy performance; the small bottom-k advantage over reservoir does not test any listed version.
